subdomain: 4.5 Optimize token usage, latency, and cost-performance trade-offs

en.question: For a hypothetical supported deployment, processing a particular eligible prefix normally costs 1 budget unit, a cache write costs 1.4, and a cache read costs 0.2. One workload class uses each prefix once; another uses each identical prefix five times within its valid cache window. Suffix costs and quality are equal. Which policy minimizes these prefix-processing costs?

options.text: Cache both classes because the cache-read price is below the ordinary-input price.
options.note: The one-use class never earns a read saving and costs 1.4 rather than 1 unit when cached. Read pricing alone omits the write that must first be amortized.

options.text: Cache the five-use class and leave the one-use class uncached.
options.note: Five uncached uses cost 5 units; one write plus four reads costs 1.4 + 4 × 0.2 = 2.2. One-use prefixes cost less uncached, so this workload-specific policy minimizes both classes under the supplied hypothetical rates.

options.text: Cache the one-use class and leave the five-use class uncached.
options.note: This pays an unrecovered write premium for one-use prefixes and misses reusable-prefix savings on five-use prefixes. It selects the more expensive treatment for both classes.

options.text: Cache neither class because a cache write costs more than ordinary processing.
options.note: The write premium is real, but four inexpensive reads more than recover it in the five-use class. Comparing only the first use ignores the measured reuse within the valid cache lifetime.
